questions.text: Which Celtic festival did Halloween come from?
questions.explanation: Samhain marked the end of the harvest and the start of winter for the Celts. Halloween inherited several of its ideas about the otherworld.

questions.text: At what time of year was Samhain celebrated?
options: At the end of the harvest, around October 31
questions.explanation: Samhain was held as the harvest ended, around October 31. People believed the veil between the living and the dead grew thinner that night.

questions.text: Which Christian feast overlapped these traditions and gave us the name All Hallows’ Eve?
questions.explanation: All Saints’ Day (All Hallows) is celebrated on November 1. The evening before, All Hallows’ Eve, was later shortened to Halloween.

questions.text: In Celtic tradition, what happened to the world of the dead during Samhain?
options: It was sealed for a year
The veil between worlds grew thinner
questions.explanation: People believed the boundary between the living and the spirits grew thinner at Samhain, so they held rites of protection and left offerings.

questions.text: What did the Celts use at Samhain to ward off or guide spirits?
questions.explanation: They lit bonfires and sometimes disguised themselves. Those practices later influenced jack-o’-lanterns and Halloween costumes.

questions.text: Why are pumpkins carved at Halloween?
options: To roast them on a bonfire
To mark houses that give out candy
To make lanterns that scare spirits away
questions.explanation: Jack-o’-lanterns are set in windows or on porches to give light and, in folklore, to keep unfriendly spirits away.

questions.text: What are children asking for when they say “trick or treat”?
options: A magic trick or a story
Candy, or else they will play a prank
questions.explanation: Trick-or-treat means a prank or a treat: the treat is candy. If there is none, the joke is a small (usually pretend) trick.

questions.text: Where does the custom of dressing up on this night come from?
options: Celtic rites so spirits would not recognize people
questions.explanation: At Samhain people covered themselves or wore disguises to blend in with spirits. That idea became Halloween costumes.

questions.text: Before pumpkins, what did people in Ireland and Scotland mostly carve?
questions.explanation: Turnips were the usual lantern vegetable. In America the pumpkin was larger and easier to carve, so it replaced the turnip.

questions.text: Which colors are classically tied to Halloween?
questions.explanation: Orange recalls pumpkins and autumn; black recalls night and mystery. Together they became the holiday’s usual palette.

questions.text: Who was Stingy Jack in the jack-o’-lantern legend?
options: A farmer who invented the pumpkin
A blacksmith who tricked the devil and wandered with a lantern
The first child to ask for candy
A Celtic king who banned fire
questions.explanation: Jack tricked the devil and, after death, was welcomed neither in heaven nor in hell. He wandered with a coal inside a turnip: the jack-o’-lantern.

questions.text: In folklore, which creature has no reflection in a mirror?
questions.explanation: Legend says vampires cast no reflection. It is one of the classic signs used to recognize them in stories and films.

questions.text: What transformation is linked to the werewolf?
options: It turns into a bat at nightfall
It becomes a wolf, especially under a full moon
questions.explanation: A werewolf (lycanthrope) shifts from human form to wolf. In many stories the trigger is a full moon.

questions.text: Why are black cats tied to Halloween?
options: Because superstitions linked them to witches and bad luck
Because they only come out on October 31
Because they are Ireland’s official symbol
questions.explanation: For centuries in Europe, people believed witches kept black cats or even turned into them. That superstition stuck to Halloween.

questions.text: What is a “restless soul” in the legends of this night?
options: The spirit of someone who cannot find rest
A candle that will not go out
The still-living owner of a haunted house
questions.explanation: A restless soul is a ghost that has not been able to move on. Halloween stories say those presences draw closer to the living.

questions.text: When is Día de Muertos celebrated in Mexico?
options: On the first Monday in October
questions.explanation: November 1 honors deceased children and November 2 honors adults. The dates overlap All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day.

questions.text: What is placed on a Día de Muertos ofrenda?
options: Photos, marigold flowers, food, and items the loved one enjoyed
questions.explanation: The ofrenda invites the soul to visit. It holds a portrait, cempasúchil marigolds, pan de muerto, water, salt, and things they liked in life.

questions.text: Which Japanese festival honors ancestors with lanterns and dances?
questions.explanation: Obon is a summer festival that welcomes ancestral spirits with altars, dances, and lanterns.

questions.text: In China, the Hungry Ghost Festival is dedicated to…
options: Spirits who have no one to offer them rituals
questions.explanation: It is believed that in that month, spirits without family walk the world. Food and incense are offered to calm and honor them.

questions.text: Besides Mexico, which country has a strong tradition of honoring the dead in early November?
options: Guatemala, with the giant kites of Sumpango
questions.explanation: In Sumpango, Guatemala, giant kites are flown on November 1. Their colors and the wind are said to connect the living and the dead.
